terms.def: Oxygen used by microbes to break down organic matter in water. The main measure of effluent strength.
Receiver for turbine exhaust steam (≈3 bar g) that feeds the steriliser and process.
Oxygen needed to chemically oxidise all organic matter. Always higher than BOD.
The main mill product: clarified, purified and dried oil from the mesocarp.
Press oil mixed with hot dilution water before clarification.
Ratio of carotene to oxidation products. High DOBI (≥2.5) means the oil bleaches easily.
Malaysian regulator that licenses mill effluent and air emissions.
Thick-shelled palm fruit type with low oil content.
The bunch stalk left after threshing. Used for mulch, compost or biomass fuel.
Fatty acids split from the oil by lipase or heat. A key CPO quality measure (≤5%).
The harvested oil palm bunch, the mill's raw material.
The fibrous part of the press cake, burned as boiler fuel.
Kernel produced as a percentage of FFB processed.
The seed inside the nut; source of palm kernel oil.
Enzyme in the fruit that splits oil into FFA. Stopped by sterilisation.
Water and dirt in CPO. Limit ≤0.25%.
The fleshy, oil-bearing outer layer of the fruitlet.
Government agency for the palm oil industry; publisher of the Palm Oil Mill Pocketbook.
Solids in fibre or sludge that are not oil, used to express oil losses on a dry basis.
The shell plus kernel, after the mesocarp has been pressed off.
CPO produced as a percentage of FFB processed.
Shell-less fruit type, used as the male parent of Tenera.
Wastewater from sterilisation, clarification and hydrocyclones.
Fibre and nuts leaving the screw press.
Nut cracker with a rotor that rolls nuts against a ripple plate.
Underflow from the clarifier: water, solids and some oil.
Dura × Pisifera hybrid with a thin shell and high oil. The commercial standard.
Sterilisation cycle with three steam pressure peaks to purge air.
A bunch that still has fruit after threshing. Usually a sign of under-sterilisation.
